hero.h1: Hydro Jet Sewer Cleaning in Elmhurst, IL
hero.sub: If roots are back a few months after every rodding, the pipe walls are still covered in growth. A hydro jet scours the line clean from end to end. We camera it first and give you a flat price before we start. Our office is on York Street, downtown.

img.alt: J. Blanton Plumbing technician kneeling on a residential driveway, feeding a hydro jet hose into a sewer cleanout, with a branded service truck parked at the curb behind him

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.body: Hydro jetting clears a sewer line with a high-pressure water stream, fed through the same cleanout access point used for rodding. A specialized nozzle sprays water in every direction as it moves through the pipe, scouring grease, scale, and roots off the entire pipe wall instead of just cutting a path through the middle. It's the fix for buildup that keeps coming back after rodding, or for roots that have worked into the pipe joints. Rodding opens the line back up. Hydro jetting cleans it.

img.alt: Diagram showing how hydro jetting clears a residential sewer line, with a cross-section view of the underground pipe, jet nozzle, high-pressure water spray, and debris being flushed toward the street connection

blocks.intro: Elmhurst's postwar clay and cast iron lines are exactly the kind that build up roots and scale.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton

steps.body: Pressure matched to clay, cast iron or PVC.
A second camera pass at the price you approved.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber in shoe covers on a home's front steps with a sewer camera

blocks.body: We record the line before and after. Before, you'll usually see roots hanging from joints, grease coating the pipe or a rough, scaled surface in cast iron. After, the walls should look clean and round, with the joints and any cracks clearly visible. That second look is valuable. It tells us whether the pipe is sound enough to keep maintaining or whether a liner would be the smarter long-term choice.

blocks.h2: Hydro Jetting Questions From Elmhurst Homeowners

items.q: Is hydro jetting safe for a 1950s clay line?
items.preview: If it's intact. We check first.
items.answer: If the camera shows the clay is intact, yes. If a section is broken or collapsed, we'll recommend a [repair](/elmhurst/sewer-repair) first.

items.q: How long does hydro jetting take?
items.answer: Usually a few hours for a typical home, including both camera passes.

items.preview: No, but it slows them down.
items.answer: No. Roots can return through an open joint. Jetting clears them more thoroughly, and a liner seals the joints for good.

items.q: Can jetting help a slow kitchen drain?
items.answer: Yes. Decades of grease in a kitchen line is one of the best uses for jetting.
